video.title: These Genius Business Ideas Are Hidden All Over America

summary: Chris Koerner and his long-time friend Nick trade 'hidden' state-by-state business ideas: beach weddings as a service, reselling merch from cult regional attractions that don't sell online (the Texas Snacks/Buc-ee's model), rentable movie vehicles and TV-location tours, drive-a-tank experiences, goat grazing for brush clearing, and reselling unclaimed or left-behind items. Chris also announces a 'business in 50 states in 50 days' YouTube series inspired by Ryan Trahan and frames paid shout-outs on big creators as cheap media buying. They close on Meta's earnings and why small home-service businesses wrongly conclude Facebook ads don't work. Key takeaway: look for proven local models (experiences, middleman/brokering, unsold merch) and copy them into other markets, using cheap targeted ads or content for distribution.

ideas.name: Beach weddings as a service (no venue)
ideas.one_liner: Packaged outdoor beach weddings (location knowledge, chairs, arch, photos, officiant) without owning a venue.
ideas.customer: Couples wanting a beach/outdoor wedding in a destination area
ideas.problem: Couples don't know which beaches need licences, have good sunsets, less seaweed/wind, and don't want to organise rentals
ideas.offer: Done-for-you wedding package: location selection, ~100 chair rental, arch, photos, vows

pricing.notes: Speakers are inconsistent on volume (hundred-something vs 1,000 weddings a year).

ideas.delivery: Operator and crew set up at chosen beach locations; physical event delivery.

acquisition.how: Inbound SEO/ads for destination weddings could be automated; not stated in the video.

onboarding.how: Booking forms and package selection automatable; couples usually want a human planner.

delivery.how: Physical setup, photography and officiating on site every time.

uk_applicability.notes: UK beach weddings are limited by weather and by the rule that legal ceremonies must be at approved venues in England; celebrant-led ceremonies on beaches exist (e.g. Cornwall, Scotland has more freedom).

quotes.text: This guy started the business with $20,000. It does $3 million a year. It's very profitable. It's a wedding service.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

quotes.text: It's a beach wedding as a service, a package. $1,500 to $3,500 per wedding.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: White-glove destination experience planner
ideas.one_liner: Be the go-to organiser for trips to a popular destination (e.g. Vegas bachelor/bachelorette parties): hotel, parties, clubs arranged end to end.
ideas.problem: Planning a destination trip is time-consuming
ideas.delivery: Planner books venues and coordinates; mostly desk work plus local relationships.

onboarding.how: Intake forms and AI itinerary drafts.

delivery.how: Bookings can be agent-assisted; on-the-ground issues need humans.

support.how: Live trip issues need a human.

uk_applicability.notes: Works for UK stag/hen destinations; package-travel regulations may apply if bundling travel and accommodation.

risks: Package Travel Regulations liability if bundling

quotes.text: You could do a service where you're like, I'll arrange everything for you. the hotel you stay at, the parties you go to, the clubs
quotes.speaker: Nick

ideas.name: Online reseller of merch from cult regional attractions (Texas Snacks model)
ideas.one_liner: Buy merch/products at full retail from beloved local brands that don't sell online and resell them nationally online.
ideas.customer: Fans and tourists of cult regional brands (Buc-ee's, Lambert's Cafe, Big Texan Steak Ranch) who live far away
ideas.problem: Beloved brands have no e-commerce store, so fans can't buy merch remotely
ideas.offer: Online store selling the brand's merchandise and products

pricing.model: Retail markup over full in-store price
pricing.notes: Buyer pays full retail at the checkout; margin from markup.

acquisition_channels.details: Implied: fans searching for the brand's products online where the brand has no store.

ideas.delivery: Team physically picks and pays for goods in store, brings to warehouse, lists and ships (Texas Snacks has thousands of SKUs).
unit_economics_claims: Texas Snacks sold hundreds of thousands of units
Big Texan sells 250,000 t-shirts a year
Big Texan grosses $16-20M a year from one location

acquisition.how: Inbound search and marketplace listings run unattended.

delivery.how: Physical buying in store and fulfilment; a 3PL helps but sourcing is manual.

uk_applicability.notes: Equivalent cult UK brands/attractions exist; reselling branded goods can raise trademark issues if presented as official.

risks: Brand can launch its own e-commerce (Big Texan already ships online)
Thin margins buying at full retail

quotes.text: I'm going to go to Bies. I'm going to buy everything at full retail and I'm going to resell it. And he starts his company
quotes.speaker: Nick

quotes.text: These guys do tens of millions of dollars per year per location. And they have t-shirts and they do not sell online.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Print-on-demand merch licensing/fulfilment for restaurants and attractions
ideas.one_liner: Offer a brand a hands-off licensing deal: you run print-on-demand merch and fulfilment, they just link it from their site.
ideas.business_model: Licensing / revenue share on merch sales
ideas.customer: Restaurants and attractions with strong brands but no online merch (e.g. Lambert's Cafe)
ideas.problem: Brands leave online merch revenue on the table and don't want the work
ideas.offer: Done-for-you online merch store with on-demand printing and fulfilment

acquisition_channels.details: Direct outreach to the brand owner proposing a licensing deal.

ideas.delivery: Print-on-demand provider prints and ships; operator manages the store.

acquisition.how: Deal-making with brand owners is relationship sales; cold email to limited companies is legal in the UK but closing needs a human.

onboarding.how: Store setup from brand assets can be largely automated.

billing.how: Shop checkout and automatic royalty reports.

uk_applicability.notes: Print-on-demand and licensing work the same in the UK.

risks: Brand may decline or do it themselves

quotes.text: Look, just throw it up on your website. I'll do all the on demand printing. We'll we'll take care of the fulfillment.
quotes.speaker: Nick

ideas.name: Goat grazing brokerage (goats as a service middleman)
ideas.one_liner: Sell brush/land clearing by goats to landowners and municipalities, borrowing goats and trailers from local goat farmers instead of owning them.
ideas.business_model: Per-acre service fee; middleman margin between farmer and customer
ideas.customer: Rural landowners needing brush clearing; fire departments/municipalities for wildfire prevention
ideas.problem: Manual clearing is very expensive (claimed $28,000/acre) and machines are disruptive
ideas.offer: Goats delivered, temporary electric fencing put up, land cleared, goats collected

pricing.notes: Chris suggests charging $500 an acre as middleman.

acquisition_channels.details: Copy forestry-mulching playbook: Meta ads to rural zip codes, 35+, interest in Tractor Supply; viral time-lapse goat videos.

quote.text: he uses meta ads only to zip codes that have rural like large tracks of land 35 years and older and people that show an interest in tractor supply.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Website plus Google ads for land/brush clearing.
Supply side: goat farms found on Facebook Marketplace (90 miles of Dallas).

ideas.delivery: Farmer's goats and animal trailer, temporary electric fence; operator coordinates.
unit_economics_claims: Fire departments pay $500-$1,000/acre for goats vs $28,000/acre manual (CalMatters)
ideas.startup_cost: Low: no goats owned; website and ads

acquisition.how: Paid ads and inbound lead forms run with little human input; government contracts need bidding.

onboarding.how: Quote by acreage via form; site check maybe needed.

delivery.how: Physical transport and fencing by farmer; coordination is human.

uk_applicability.notes: Conservation grazing exists in the UK; wildfire demand is lower; animal movement rules (APHA holding numbers, movement reporting) apply.

risks: Government contracts have long sales cycles and bidding

quotes.text: fire departments will hire them and pay them $500 to $1,000 an acre to load up their animal trailer full of goats
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

quotes.text: So if you want to play middleman or woman, you go acquire customers, put up a website, Facebook ads, Google ads, what have you.

tactics.name: Find cult local brands with no online store
steps: Run a deep-research prompt to list beloved regional restaurants/attractions (Lambert's, Big Texan type)
Check whether they sell merch online
Either resell their goods (buy at retail) or pitch a licensing deal where you handle print-on-demand and fulfilment

quote.text: Someone needs to run a deep research prompt and find all of the the throat rolls, the Lambert's cafes, the big Texan, all of those of the world
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Borrowed-supply service brokerage (goats)
steps: Search Facebook Marketplace for goat farms within ~90 miles
Arrange to borrow goats and the farmer's animal trailer
Build a website and run Facebook/Google ads for brush clearing
Charge ~$500/acre, put up temporary electric fencing, return goats same day
Film time-lapse videos for organic virality

tactics.name: Meta targeting for rural landowners
steps: Target only rural zip codes with large tracts of land
Age 35+
Interest in Tractor Supply
Use instant-form leads and videos, never pictures

quote.text: You need instant form leads. Like you need videos, never pictures ever.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Buy reach via charity donation shout-outs
steps: Find a mega-creator running a charity drive with shout-outs for donors over a threshold
Donate (e.g. $5,000) with a message promoting your project
Compare effective CPM (~$10 on ~5M views) with other media

quote.text: if you donated 5,000 or more, he would shout you out on his video.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Hire an agency with a planned exit
steps: Tell the agency upfront you plan to fire them in 3 months
Ask them to Loom-record everything they do for you
Learn the channel so you can hold future agencies accountable

quote.text: Hire an agency, but tell them upfront, my goal is to fire you in 3 months and I'd like you to loom everything that you do for me
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Facebook for home services: retarget and plant seeds
steps: Put a Meta pixel on the website
Retarget visitors (high intent, ~7 touches needed)
Use founder-led video ads
Use Google for hot, high-intent demand and Facebook for awareness/retargeting

lessons.lesson: Look for proven single-location businesses and replicate the model in other markets; experiences and middleman services travel well.

quote.text: there are these types of beloved tourist kind of attractions in different states.
quote.speaker: Nick

lessons.lesson: Middleman models let you sell a service without owning the supply: borrow assets from people who already have them.

quote.text: You don't necessarily hold the inventory, but you're the guy or gal who finds the buyer and the seller and places

lessons.lesson: Price against the customer's real alternative: goat grazing at $1,000 an acre versus $28,000 manual clearing leaves room for a middleman.
Many exciting businesses are badly under-marketed; consistent unedited content alone could grow them.

quote.text: what's the downside to just point shoot, upload, point, shoot, upload. They don't even have to do any editing really.

lessons.lesson: Reframe a perceived curse (fame, attention) as an asset to monetise.
Small businesses abandon channels because they aren't desperate enough; good is the enemy of great.

quote.text: They're probably just not desperate enough. Like they have other customer acquisition strategies that are working fine and good is the enemy to great
